Q1: Titanium dioxide is associated with known hazards, categorized at Tier 1 for Carcinogenicity, Mutagenicity, and Reproductive (CMR) hazards, as well as Organ and Systemic (OGN) hazards. Further assessment, an expanded perspective (Tier 2), indicates potential environmental (ENV), endocrine disruption (EDC), inhalation (IHL), and dermal/eye (SKN) hazards. Oral exposure (ORL) is considered a demonstrated low to moderate hazard (Tier 3).
Q2: Titanium dioxide is recognized on several authoritative lists of concern. It is classified by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) as Group 2B, indicating it is possibly carcinogenic to humans, and is also identified by The Endocrine Disruption Exchange (TEDX) as a potential endocrine disruptor.
Q3: Titanium dioxide is an extensively studied and exceptionally well-characterized chemical, with over 700,000 scientific literature references, significantly surpassing the typical number for most substances. Its hazard profile is considered comprehensive, supported by its specific molecular formula (O2Ti), classification as a 'Small Molecule,' and the absence of any data-deficient (Tier 4) hazard classifications.
